cross_industry.statement: A utility said its regulated rate base will grow 8% a year through 2028.
A payments company's largest bank partner said it will move its card processing to a competitor next year.
A grocery chain said food inflation slowed to 2% in its stores last quarter.
A chip equipment maker said China accounted for 40% of its sales last year.
An airline pilots' union voted to authorise a strike.
A cement maker's CEO said demand is very strong.
Unnamed sources said the regulator is preparing to fine the bank about $1 billion.
The insurer's chief actuary said catastrophe losses in the third quarter were the highest in a decade.
A brokerage downgraded the miner to sell, citing falling copper prices.
A software company said 15 of the Fortune 100 now use its product; no revenue was given.
The government extended a 25% tariff on imported steel through 2027.
The drug maker presented new data at a medical conference showing its drug cut hospital stays by a third.

questions.question: What will the utility's 2027 rate base be?
Will the regulator fine the bank by the end of 2026?
Will the 25% steel tariff still be in force on 2027-12-31?
What will the payments company's revenue from its largest bank partner be in FY2027?
What share of the chip equipment maker's FY2026 sales will come from China?
Will the airline pilots strike before the end of 2026?
What will global copper prices average in 2027?
Will the drug maker's drug be added to the main clinical guideline by mid-2027?
